words.definition: The occurrence of events by chance in a happy or beneficial way.
words.example: Finding that little café was pure serendipity.

words.definition: Pleasantly smooth and musical to hear.
words.example: She had a mellifluous voice that calmed the whole room.

words.definition: Lasting for a very short time.
words.example: The beauty of the sunset was ephemeral.

words.definition: The pleasant, earthy smell after rain falls on dry ground.
words.example: We stepped outside and breathed in the petrichor.

words.definition: Full of or giving off light; bright or shining.
words.example: The luminous moon lit up the whole beach.

words.definition: Hopeful and idealistic in a way that is not practical or realistic.
words.example: His quixotic plan was to visit every country in a single year.

words.definition: Describing a happy, peaceful time in the past.
words.example: She remembered the halcyon summers of her childhood.

words.definition: Able to express ideas clearly and persuasively.
words.example: Her eloquent speech moved the audience to tears.

words.definition: The ability to recover quickly from difficulties.
words.example: The team showed great resilience after losing the first game.

words.definition: Seeming to be everywhere at the same time.
words.example: Smartphones have become ubiquitous.

words.definition: The realisation that every passer-by has a life as vivid and complex as your own.
words.example: Watching the crowd at the station, he was struck by a feeling of sonder.

words.definition: A strong desire to travel and explore the world.
words.example: Her wanderlust took her across three continents.

words.definition: Kind, generous and well-meaning.
words.example: A benevolent neighbour left groceries on our doorstep.

words.definition: The quality of being open, honest and direct.
words.example: I appreciated the candour of her feedback.

words.definition: Showing care and effort in one's work or duties.
words.example: A diligent student, he reviewed his notes every night.

words.definition: Bubbly and lively; full of energy and enthusiasm.
words.example: Her effervescent personality made every party more fun.

words.definition: Fond of company; sociable.
words.example: Gregarious by nature, he knew everyone at the party.

words.definition: Too great or extreme to be described in words.
words.example: Standing at the summit, she felt an ineffable joy.

words.definition: To place two things side by side to compare or contrast them.
words.example: The exhibition juxtaposes old photographs with modern ones.

words.definition: Relating to or resulting from motion.
words.example: The dancers filled the stage with kinetic energy.

words.definition: A complicated network of paths in which it is easy to get lost.
words.example: The old town was a labyrinth of narrow streets.

words.definition: Showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise.
words.example: She kept meticulous records of every experiment.

words.definition: A sentimental longing for a period in the past.
words.example: The old song filled him with nostalgia.

words.definition: Not aware of or not concerned about what is happening around you.
words.example: He was oblivious to the rain while reading his book.

words.definition: A solution or remedy for all problems or difficulties.
words.example: Technology is not a panacea for every problem.

words.definition: Representing the most perfect or typical example of something.
words.example: Fish and chips by the sea is the quintessential seaside meal.

words.definition: A state of being pleasantly lost in one's thoughts; a daydream.
words.example: The doorbell broke her reverie.

words.definition: The state of being alone, especially when it is peaceful and pleasant.
words.example: He enjoyed the solitude of early morning walks.

words.definition: Holding firmly to something; determined and persistent.
words.example: The tenacious puppy would not let go of the rope.

words.definition: Impossible to fully understand or measure.
words.example: The size of the universe is unfathomable.

words.definition: Attractively lively and full of spirit.
words.example: Her vivacious laugh could be heard across the room.

words.definition: Playfully unusual or fanciful, often in an amusing way.
words.example: The café was decorated in a whimsical style with teapot lamps.

words.definition: Having or showing great energy or enthusiasm for a cause or goal.
words.example: The zealous volunteers worked through the night.

words.definition: Having mixed feelings or contradictory ideas about something.
words.example: She felt ambivalent about moving to a new city.

words.definition: A harsh, jarring mixture of sounds.
words.example: The cacophony of car horns filled the street.

words.definition: Cheerful and full of energy.
words.example: The ebullient crowd cheered as the team arrived.

words.definition: Very attentive to accuracy and detail; hard to please.
words.example: He was fastidious about keeping his desk tidy.

words.definition: A very fine, delicate substance, like the threads of a spider's web.
words.example: Morning dew clung to the gossamer between the branches.

words.definition: Excessive pride or self-confidence.
words.example: His hubris led him to ignore every warning.

words.definition: Extremely happy, peaceful or picturesque.
words.example: They spent an idyllic week in a cottage by the lake.

words.definition: Feeling or expressing great happiness and triumph.
words.example: The jubilant fans danced in the streets.

words.definition: Sluggish and lacking in energy.
words.example: The heat made everyone feel lethargic.

words.definition: Lacking interest or excitement; dull and ordinary.
words.example: She found joy even in mundane tasks like washing up.

words.definition: Wicked or criminal.
words.example: The villain had a nefarious plan to steal the crown jewels.

words.definition: Rich, luxurious and lavish.
words.example: The hotel lobby was opulent, with marble floors and gold lamps.

words.definition: Engaged in deep or serious thought.
words.example: He stared out of the window with a pensive look.

words.definition: Noisy, energetic and hard to control.
words.example: The rambunctious puppies knocked over the plant pot.

words.definition: Cheerfully optimistic, especially in a difficult situation.
words.example: She remained sanguine about her chances of winning.

words.definition: Lasting only for a short time; temporary.
words.example: The town has a large transient population of tourists.

words.definition: Given great respect because of age, wisdom or character.
words.example: The venerable oak had stood in the square for centuries.

words.definition: Having a feeling of gentle sadness and longing.
words.example: She gave a wistful smile as the train pulled away.

words.definition: Self-confidence and calmness, especially in a demanding situation.
words.example: She handled the tricky questions with aplomb.

words.definition: Relating to the pleasant aspects of the countryside and country life.
words.example: The painting showed a bucolic scene of sheep in a meadow.

words.definition: Kept secret or done secretively.
words.example: They held clandestine meetings in the old library.

words.definition: Showing fearlessness and determination.
words.example: The dauntless explorer pressed on through the storm.

words.definition: A person or thing that is mysterious or difficult to understand.
words.example: The new neighbour remained something of an enigma.

words.definition: Intense happiness; also, the ability to find just the right words.
words.example: They lived in perfect felicity in their little house.

words.definition: Glowing with heat; or full of strong emotion.
words.example: The incandescent lava lit up the night sky.

words.definition: Relaxed and slow, without effort or energy.
words.example: We spent a languid afternoon floating in the pool.

words.definition: Attractive and impressive through being colourful or splendid.
words.example: The peacock was resplendent in blue and green.
